reran: cmd.sh on the integration build, the base and 2.13.18: compiles, then StackOverflowError, as recorded; 2.12.20 the same. Scala 3.7.4 prints 2. -Xprint:specialize on the integration build shows C.m$mcI$sp calling C.super.m$mcI$sp[X], bound to the forwarder declared in the generic trait T0, which calls m, which C overrides.
user_impact: A class that fixes the type argument of a specialized trait and overrides a method that has its own type parameter, calling super: trait Fold[@specialized(Int) A] { def foldAll[Z](z: Z)(f: (Z, A) => Z): Z }; class IntFold extends Fold[Int] { override def foldAll[Z](z: Z)(f: (Z, Int) => Z) = f(super.foldAll(z)(f), 1) } overflows the stack on the integration build (I ran it). Only a trait parent: with a class parent the same program prints 2. Collection-like specialized traits with fold/map style methods are the natural victims.
fixability: clear cut, as a wider fix on retronym/scala#354 rather than a separate pull request. #354 handles Apply(Select(Super)) under hasNewParents; a call with type arguments is Apply(TypeApply(Select(Super))) and goes to the TypeApply case, which looks the variant up in the stale type of the Super tree and selects it by symbol, so mixin calls the generic trait's forwarder. Rebuilding and retyping the Super qualifier there (or applying the override lookup that #433 added to transformSelect) is the same idea in the neighbouring case. Compatibility cost as for #354.
links: B2 (retronym/scala#354) and B13 (retronym/scala#433): same family; the fix on the integration build does not reach calls with type arguments. NW3 is the abstract override variant. GE1 is unrelated.
note: The gap is wider than the finding says: with the method type parameter itself @specialized (trait T1[@specialized(Int) B] { def m[@specialized(Int) X](x: X, b: B) }, class C1 extends T1[Int] with super.m[X](x, b)) the call also overflows on the integration build, for an Int and for a String argument. The test in #354 covers that shape only with a class parent (B3/I3), where the JVM's invokespecial resolution hides the wrong symbol. The test rows to add are trait parent with an unspecialized and with a specialized method type parameter, with inferred type arguments.
